- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to correct for momentum decay.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.36) and model is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 1–4% to match sentiment-driven upward bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply a +1.5%–3% bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment is volatile or erratic (alternating 0.18–0.53), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values or apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% over 30-day horizon, model likely missed a structural trend; apply +2–5% bias to next forecast if sentiment remains bullish.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven mean reversion in late horizon (last 7–10 days); if sentiment is high then drops, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect cooling momentum.
